summary: Validated (the first patch failed on malformed hunk headers and was re-issued cleanly, then validate --run <run> --submission update22.json → valid=true). New direction on the reload path, recorded as a low-severity implementation mismatch rather than a safety defect. ReloadConfig writes the new configuration and then notifies the leader and follower channels only when the heartbeat timeout decreased, with comments saying the leader's replication loops must see a shorter heartbeat timeout and a follower must update its current timer (api.go:733-739). The follower consumes that notification by re-arming its timer at once (raft.go:208-212); the candidate consumes the same notification through a branch whose stated purpose is to adopt a changed election timeout — it compares its captured value with the configured one and re-arms if they differ (raft.go:423-427). Since the notification is gated on the *heartbeat* timeout, a reload that changes the election timeout alone (even lowering it) never reaches that comparison, so a candidacy in progress keeps its original timer and only the next candidacy reads the new value at entry. Graded honestly: no security or safety consequence — the timer only bounds when another election attempt starts and the new value applies to that attempt — and the reloadable-configuration documentation states what the field means without promising when a change takes effect (unlike the trailing-logs entry, which names its effect point), so this is not a breached written duty; the strongest honest reading is that the refresh branch exists for a case its only wake source cannot deliver. Recorded as one Behavior/Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation and an active question with a discriminator (a candidate with a long election timeout plus an election-timeout-only reload, observing when the candidacy restarts), with counterevidence kept explicit, including that any reload decreasing the heartbeat timeout does wake the branch and that the delay is bounded to one attempt.
